news_highlights.title: OpenCode Hacked: User credentials leaked
news_highlights.why_it_matters: OpenCode says a breach tied to a large-scale distillation attack hit 1.4% of OpenCode Console users, who were emailed, and the incident is still ongoing. OpenCode is on today's GitHub Trending list too. If you use OpenCode Console, check your email and consider rotating the provider keys you connected.

news_highlights.title: DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash-1017
news_highlights.why_it_matters: An MIT-licensed open-weights update that reports big agentic-coding gains (Terminal-Bench 4.0 in the Claude Code harness: 42.3, up from 31.2) with shorter outputs and a 1M-token context. It could be a cheaper model to put behind coding agents.

news_highlights.title: Linus Torvalds on AI-assisted kernel contributions
news_highlights.why_it_matters: How the Linux kernel treats AI-assisted patches is likely to shape contribution rules for agent-written code across open source. The thread drew 159 comments on Lobsters.

news_highlights.title: Codex Desktop continuously generates Crashpad pending dumps
news_highlights.why_it_matters: An open Codex issue reports the desktop app writing crash dumps over and over. If you run Codex Desktop, watch its disk usage until a fix lands.

news_highlights.title: Chrome and Edge are removing XSLT: what breaks and what does not
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Chromium browsers are dropping built-in XSLT, which some sites still use to style XML such as RSS/Atom feeds and sitemaps in the browser. Check whether any client sites depend on it.
